planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring with the crown at the soil surface in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this dwarf selection resents being crowded by larger neighbors.

directions: Flirt is a miniature Terra Nova Nurseries selection that stays noticeably smaller than typical border bergenias, forming a tight rosette of glossy, rounded leaves that darken to near-black through winter cold. In spring the compact clump sends up a surprising number of short, sturdy flower stalks topped with deep pink bells, often blooming more heavily per square foot than its larger-growing relatives. Because of its diminutive size it suits rock gardens, trough plantings, and the front edge of a shaded border where bigger bergenias would overwhelm the space. Divide congested clumps in spring or fall and pull off tattered old leaves to keep the small rosettes looking tidy.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this older German selection is valued for flower size rather than an unusual color.

directions: Schneekönigin ('Snow Queen') is a mid-twentieth-century selection raised by the nurseryman and garden designer Karl Foerster, notable for unusually large flowers. Rounded buds open white in early spring and gradually flush soft pink as they age, so a single flower stalk can show both colors at once over several weeks of bloom. The glossy, wavy-edged leaves stay handsome through winter and knit together into a dense, weed-suppressing clump in shaded, humus-rich ground. Remove any winter-damaged leaves in early spring just before the flower stalks begin to elongate.

common_name: Rotblum Bergenia (Red Beauty / Red Start Pigsqueak)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this early-blooming selection is sold under several names but represents a single clone.

directions: Rotblum, German for 'red flower,' was introduced by Jelitto Perennial Seeds in 1978 and is grown for bloom color that reads noticeably deeper and rosier than the pale pink of the species. Big, glossy, cabbage-like leaves turn deep burgundy through fall and winter, giving the clump strong presence even outside the bloom period. Branching flower stalks open earlier in spring than many other bergenias, carrying dense clusters of rose-red flowers that emerge from distinctive pink-green calyces. In North American nurseries the same clone is also commonly sold as 'Red Beauty' or 'Red Start.'

common_name: Irish Crimson Bergenia (Helen Dillon / Glasnevin Pigsqueak)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; this old Dublin garden selection is grown mainly for its exceptional winter leaf color and is also traded as 'Helen Dillon' or 'Glasnevin', the name under which it holds its RHS Award of Garden Merit.

directions: Irish Crimson has long been grown in Dublin gardens, originally distributed by the noted Irish gardener Helen Dillon and still occasionally sold under her name or as 'Glasnevin' as a synonym. Its narrow, upright leaves carry a pink-tinged margin and pale midrib through summer, then deepen to an intense beetroot crimson that persists all winter, among the richest winter foliage color in the genus. Nodding, deep pink flowers rise on dark stems well above the foliage in early spring, standing out against the colored leaves below. This clone has received the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit for its dependable performance in shaded borders.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; being a sported variegation, any all-green reverted growth should be cut away.

directions: Solar Flare was discovered as a branch mutation on 'Herbstblute' and was patented for its distinct, stable variegation pattern. New leaves emerge with a broad, irregular yellow margin surrounding a green center, an effect that is most vivid on fresh spring growth before softening somewhat later in the season. Large, bright pink flower clusters appear in spring, and the rounded leaves flush red once cold weather arrives, adding a second season of interest. Because the pattern originated as a genetic sport, any shoots reverting to solid green should be removed to keep the clump true to type.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun; strongest color develops on plants that are actively growing rather than stressed.

directions: Lunar Glow arose as a further sport from tissue-cultured plants of 'Solar Flare' and was patented separately for carrying yellow coloring further across the leaf than its parent. New growth emerges creamy yellow with green veining, a color retained through much of the growing season as long as the plant keeps producing fresh leaves, before the foliage shifts toward green and maroon-purple tones with cooler weather. Large, bright pink flowers open in spring on sturdy stems above the chartreuse foliage. As with other sported bergenias, occasional green reversions should be cut out to preserve the gold leaf effect.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in full sun to part shade.

directions: Tubby Andrews is grown chiefly for its foliage, with leathery, oval leaves irregularly marbled in green and cream rather than the flat green of ordinary heartleaf bergenia. The cream variegation shows strongest on young leaves and tends to green up somewhat as each leaf matures, while cool fall and winter temperatures add pink and red tones across the whole leaf surface. Clusters of soft pink, bell-shaped flowers rise on sturdy stalks in early spring and occasionally repeat sparingly into fall. It tolerates a wider range of light than most variegated perennials, performing from full sun to part shade as long as soil stays reliably moist.
